actLaundry.intro: Sort a pile of laundry into darks, lights and towels, then read care labels to pick the right water. Ask an adult before you use a washer or dryer the first time.
actLaundry.sortH: Sort the pile into three baskets.
actLaundry.dragStatic: Drag each item to a basket. Or tap an item, then tap a basket.
actLaundry.dragHint: Drag each item to a basket. Or click an item, then click a basket.
actLaundry.tapHint: Tap an item, then tap the basket it goes in.
actLaundry.pickedP: Now choose a basket for it.
actLaundry.firstTry: {a} of {n} went in the right basket on the first try.
actLaundry.everyRight: Every item is in the right basket now.
actLaundry.pickFirstP: Tap an item in the pile, then tap a basket. Or drag it over.

ok.l: Lights stay together so they stay bright.
ok.d: Darks wash together so their color stays put.
ok.t: Towels shed lint, so they get their own load.
ok.r: New bright colors can bleed in the wash, so the red jersey goes with the darks.

l.dark: Light clothes can pick up color from darks and look dingy, so lights wash with lights.
l.towel: Towels are thick and shed lint onto clothes, so clothes wash in their own load.

d.light: Dark clothes can leak color onto light ones, so darks wash with darks.
d.towel: Towels are thick and shed lint onto clothes, so clothes wash in their own load.

t.dark: Towels shed lint onto other clothes, so they get their own load.
t.light: Towels shed lint onto other clothes, so they get their own load.

r.light: A new red jersey can bleed and turn light clothes pink. New bright colors go with the darks.
r.towel: Towels shed lint, and a new red jersey can bleed color too. New bright colors go with the darks.

ltx.nob: Triangle with an X: do not use bleach.
ltx.dry: Square with a circle and {d}: tumble dry on {h} heat.
ltx.nodry: Square and circle with an X: do not use a dryer.
ltx.flat: Square with a line in it: lay the item flat to dry.
ltx.iron: Iron with {d}: iron on {h} heat. Ask an adult first.
ltx.noiron: Iron with an X: do not iron.

actLaundry.qTemp: What water temperature does this label say?
actLaundry.qTempP: Look at the washtub. More dots mean hotter water.
actLaundry.qDry: Can this go in the dryer?
actLaundry.qDryP: Look at the square with the circle.
actLaundry.waterWhy: The washtub has {d}, which means {w} water.
actLaundry.here: Here is what the label says.
actLaundry.allDone: All sorted and read. Try it again and use the hints.
actLaundry.good1: Sorted {a} of {n} items on the first try
actLaundry.good2: Spotted that a new red jersey can bleed
actLaundry.good4: You sorted the whole pile and read every label
actLaundry.tipDots: Count the dots on the washtub. {d} means {w} water.
actLaundry.tipX: An X over the dryer symbol means no dryer.
actLaundry.tipDefault: Check the care label every time before you wash.
actLaundry.askAdult: Ask an adult before you use a washer or dryer the first time.
